name: Dalit feminism
summary: Dalit feminism holds that Dalit women are oppressed by caste, gender and class together, so neither the largely upper-caste women's movement nor a male-led Dalit movement speaks for them. It builds on Ambedkar's analysis of caste and brahmanical patriarchy and develops a standpoint theory from Dalit women's own experience. Its programme asks for enforced equal rights, land titled to women, an end to bonded labour, manual scavenging and the devadasi system, representation, and an end to impunity for caste-sexual violence.
scope: The Indian Dalit feminist tradition: Sharmila Rege's Dalit feminist standpoint and brahmanical patriarchy (1990s), Gopal Guru's 'Dalit women talk differently', the National Federation of Dalit Women (Ruth Manorama) and the 2006 Delhi and Hague declarations, with Ambedkar as the founding background through Dalit feminist readings. Answers rest only on what these Dalit feminist texts and programmes state; the wider left, feminism in general and Ambedkar's other positions are not borrowed.
